lines.say: Homeostasis only works if every link in the pathway does its job.

draw.alt: Chain of the stimulus-response pathway with the gland link broken

lines.say: A gland can make too little hormone. That's hyposecretion.
Or too much hormone. That's hypersecretion.
Or the target cells stop responding, or feedback stops switching it off.
Type 1 diabetes is autoimmune. The immune system destroys the beta cells.
So little or no insulin is made. That's a gland fault.
Cells take up little glucose, so blood glucose stays high. Hyperglycaemia.
Kidney carriers can only work so fast. Extra glucose stays in the filtrate.

draw.alt: Glucose carriers are all busy, so extra glucose is left in the filtrate

lines.say: That glucose holds water back. Lots of urine, and the person feels very thirsty.
Cells starve, so they break down fat. That can make acidic ketones.
The missing piece is insulin, so replace it with injections or a pump.
Too much insulin causes hypoglycaemia. Fast-acting sugar fixes it.
In type 2, insulin is made, but target cells respond poorly. A jammed lock.
Data rule: high glucose, low insulin? Look at the gland.
High glucose and high insulin? Look at the target cells.
Thyroxine sets the metabolic rate. It needs iodine to be made.
Hypothalamus releases TRH. Pituitary releases TSH. Thyroid releases thyroxine.

draw.alt: Hypothalamus to pituitary to thyroid; high thyroxine feeds back to reduce TSH

lines.say: High thyroxine switches off TRH and TSH. That's negative feedback.
In Graves' disease, antibodies bind the TSH receptors and switch the thyroid on.
Feedback can't switch the antibodies off. Like a doorbell jammed on.
So thyroxine is high, but TSH is low.
Everything speeds up: hot, sweaty, fast heart, weight loss. Maybe a goitre.
Hypothyroidism is the opposite: tired, cold, weight gain.
Diabetes insipidus is about ADH and water, not glucose.
Central: not enough ADH is made. Nephrogenic: the kidneys don't respond.
Either way, collecting ducts keep little water. Huge volumes of dilute urine.

draw.alt: Normal urine volume compared with a much larger volume in diabetes insipidus

lines.say: Synthetic ADH treats the central form, but not the nephrogenic form.
Too much ADH does the reverse. The blood becomes too dilute.
Type 1 isn't caused by eating sugar. It's autoimmune.
Mellitus means honey, it's glucose. Insipidus is ADH and water.
Low TSH in Graves' doesn't mean an underactive thyroid.
Find the broken link, then explain each step with so or therefore.
